shortDescription.text: filterTable() reads the q query parameter at frontend/src/app/search-result/search-result.component.ts:136, trims it, and passes the raw value to DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml at line 143.

fullDescription.text: filterTable() reads the q query parameter at frontend/src/app/search-result/search-result.component.ts:136, trims it, and passes the raw value to DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml at line 143. frontend/src/app/search-result/search-result.component.html:11 binds that SafeHtml straight into [innerHTML], so a crafted search link executes attacker-supplied markup in the shop's own origin. Because login.component.ts:101 keeps the session JWT in localStorage and no Content-Security-Policy restricts script sources, the injected code reads the token and reaches any API the victim can reach.

shortDescription.text: A case-insensitive search of the entire frontend source tree for content-security-policy and frame-ancestors returns zero hits, so the application ships neither a meta-tag policy nor any client-side policy configuration.

fullDescription.text: A case-insensitive search of the entire frontend source tree for content-security-policy and frame-ancestors returns zero hits, so the application ships neither a meta-tag policy nor any client-side policy configuration. Without a policy there is no script-source allowlist and no frame-ancestors restriction, which is what lets the six DomSanitizer bypasses in this component escalate from markup injection to full token exfiltration: injected script may load and contact arbitrary external origins, and the application may be framed for clickjacking.

shortDescription.text: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:101 writes the session JWT to localStorage, line 135 stores the user's email address there when remember-me is selected, and frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:16 reads the token back to build the Authorization header for every API call.

fullDescription.text: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:101 writes the session JWT to localStorage, line 135 stores the user's email address there when remember-me is selected, and frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:16 reads the token back to build the Authorization header for every API call. localStorage is readable by any script running in the origin, so each of the markup-injection sinks in this same component converts into durable session theft rather than a transient defacement. frontend/src/app/chatbot/chat-conversation/chat-conversation.component.ts:107 additionally persists complete chat transcripts through ConversationStorageService, exposing conversation content to the same scripts.

shortDescription.text: AdminGuard grants the administration route when payload.data.role equals the admin role at frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:54, where payload comes from jwtDecode at line 38 — a decoder that parses the token body and verifies no signature.

fullDescription.text: AdminGuard grants the administration route when payload.data.role equals the admin role at frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:54, where payload comes from jwtDecode at line 38 — a decoder that parses the token body and verifies no signature. A user who rewrites the base64 payload of the token held in their own localStorage to carry role admin passes the guard, loads AdministrationComponent, and drives its privileged operations including the user listing and the feedback deletion at frontend/src/app/administration/administration.component.ts:104. Whether the API server independently re-authorizes those calls cannot be observed from this component; the client-side guard itself supplies no authorization.

shortDescription.text: An attacker reads `data/static/users.yml` in the public repository and finds six seeded administrator passwords in plaintext: admin/admi**** (8 chars) at line 3, support at line 115, J12934 at line 141, wurstbrot at line 150, testing at line 272, and demo at line 215.

shortDescription.text: The OAuth callback derives each federated user's shop password from a public identifier.

fullDescription.text: The OAuth callback derives each federated user's shop password from a public identifier. frontend/src/app/oauth/oauth.component.ts:30 computes it as btoa(profile.email.split('').reverse().join('')) and registers the account with that value, and line 46 submits the identical expression to userService.login as the authentication credential. shortDescription.text: An attacker who obtains the long-lived DOCKERHUB_TOKEN held in repository secrets authenticates to Docker Hub as the project and pushes a backdoored bkimminich/juice-shop:latest.

fullDescription.text: An attacker who obtains the long-lived DOCKERHUB_TOKEN held in repository secrets authenticates to Docker Hub as the project and pushes a backdoored bkimminich/juice-shop:latest. The workflow publishes with push: true and emits no provenance attestation or signature, so a pulled image carries nothing a consumer can check against the real build. Every downstream docker pull and docker-compose deployment accepts the impersonated artifact as the project's own.

shortDescription.text: An attacker copies the fixed base32 TOTP seed `IFTXE3SPOEYVURT2MRYGI52TKJ4HC3KH` from `data/static/users.yml:151` and generates valid six-digit codes offline for the administrator account `wurstbrot`.

fullDescription.text: An attacker copies the fixed base32 TOTP seed `IFTXE3SPOEYVURT2MRYGI52TKJ4HC3KH` from `data/static/users.yml:151` and generates valid six-digit codes offline for the administrator account `wurstbrot`. Because the same shared secret is seeded into each database rather than enrolled per instance, the attacker passes the second authentication factor on every deployment.

shortDescription.text: googleLogin() at frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148 builds the Google authorization URL with response_type=token and no state, nonce, or PKCE parameter.

fullDescription.text: googleLogin() at frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148 builds the Google authorization URL with response_type=token and no state, nonce, or PKCE parameter. The access token therefore returns in the URL fragment, where frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:257 copies window.location.href into route data and frontend/src/app/oauth/oauth.component.ts:71 splits it into parameters. Because nothing binds the returned fragment to the browser session that started the flow, an attacker can complete the callback with a token of their choosing and have the victim's browser adopt the resulting session.

shortDescription.text: An anonymous internet client completes the Socket.IO handshake on port 3000 and is accepted by the connection handler registered at line 23.

fullDescription.text: An anonymous internet client completes the Socket.IO handshake on port 3000 and is accepted by the connection handler registered at line 23. The handler installs no io.use() middleware, never reads socket.handshake.auth, and never applies the JWT check that guards the REST API, so the socket is trusted without any identity. From that socket the attacker receives every buffered challenge-solved notification and emits the state-changing notification received and verify* events.

shortDescription.text: An attacker hosts a page that auto-submits a form to POST /profile; the victim's browser attaches the token cookie that routes/updateUserProfile.ts:17 reads for authentication, no CSRF token or SameSite attribute is checked, and line 38 persists the attacker-chosen username while server.ts:183 enables permissive CORS for every origin.

When the `noSqlCommand` challenge is enabled, `routes/showProductReviews.ts:31` truncates the segment to 40 characters and concatenates it into a `$where` expression at line 36, executing the supplied text as JavaScript in the query engine. The attacker invokes the blocking sleep helper to confirm blind execution or returns all reviews regardless of product.

shortDescription.text: The repository sets package-lock=false, so no lockfile is ever generated and every npm install in CI and in the container build resolves the full transitive dependency graph fresh against the live npm registry.

fullDescription.text: The repository sets package-lock=false, so no lockfile is ever generated and every npm install in CI and in the container build resolves the full transitive dependency graph fresh against the live npm registry. An attacker who gains a momentary version window on any transitive dependency through typosquatting, maintainer account takeover, or a poisoned new release gets that version installed into the next build with no diff, no lockfile baseline, and no integrity hash to reject it.

shortDescription.text: An attacker who compromises the calibreapp/image-actions repository or its maintainer account pushes malicious code to the main branch.

fullDescription.text: An attacker who compromises the calibreapp/image-actions repository or its maintainer account pushes malicious code to the main branch. The next image-touching commit on master or develop resolves calibreapp/image-actions@main to that code and executes it on the runner with secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN passed in at line 35, letting the attacker read repository secrets available to the job and commit to the repository through the peter-evans/create-pull-request@v8 step.

shortDescription.text: After a successful data-export request, frontend/src/app/data-export/data-export.component.ts:71 opens a blank window with window.open('', '_blank', 'width=500') and writes the server-returned userData into it with document.write.

fullDescription.text: After a successful data-export request, frontend/src/app/data-export/data-export.component.ts:71 opens a blank window with window.open('', '_blank', 'width=500') and writes the server-returned userData into it with document.write. The new document inherits the shop's origin, so any HTML contained in the aggregated export — reviews, memories, and other records that originate from user submissions — is parsed as markup and executes with access to the same localStorage session token the parent page uses.

shortDescription.text: State-changing operations on sensitive resources MUST require a proven session.

fullDescription.text: State-changing operations on sensitive resources MUST require a proven session. A registration line that lacks any auth marker either trusts the URL itself or relies on a downstream check that the static signature cannot prove exists.

shortDescription.text: Neither the CI/CD Pipeline workflow nor the image-compression workflow declares a permissions: key, so every job runs with the repository default GITHUB_TOKEN scope instead of read-only contents.

fullDescription.text: Neither the CI/CD Pipeline workflow nor the image-compression workflow declares a permissions: key, so every job runs with the repository default GITHUB_TOKEN scope instead of read-only contents. That token is handed to third-party actions, including the mutable coverallsapp/github-action@v2 reference. A compromised step therefore inherits whatever the repository default grants, and the create-pull-request step in image_actions.yml proves the inherited scope already includes repository write, so the step can commit code, publish packages, or create releases.

fullDescription.text: The verifyCloseNotificationsChallenge handler marks the challenge solved when the client-supplied payload is an array longer than one element, which is the client's own assertion that it performed the action. The same pattern appears at lines 41 and 45, where the client supplies the string that is matched against the expected payload. Any socket therefore promotes global challenge state without performing the gameplay the challenge represents.

An attacker who compromises that distribution host, or who can influence DNS or TLS interception for the runner, substitutes the script and executes arbitrary code in a job that goes on to use secrets.HEROKU_API_KEY at line 371, taking over the production and staging deployment credentials.

shortDescription.text: Both build stages resolve their base image by floating reference rather than digest, so the bytes a build consumes are whatever the registry serves at that moment.

fullDescription.text: Both build stages resolve their base image by floating reference rather than digest, so the bytes a build consumes are whatever the registry serves at that moment. An attacker who compromises the upstream image or the registry path substitutes a backdoored layer, and the next docker job build bakes it into the published bkimminich/juice-shop image with no build-time signal that the base changed.

shortDescription.text: The publish step pushes exactly one tag per branch, latest or snapshot, and overwrites it on every subsequent build.

fullDescription.text: The publish step pushes exactly one tag per branch, latest or snapshot, and overwrites it on every subsequent build. After a suspected build compromise nobody can fetch the artifact that was actually deployed, because the tag now points at a newer image and no immutable version tag or digest record was ever published. The attacker's build is indistinguishable from a clean one once the next push completes.

message.text: The publish step pushes exactly one tag per branch, latest or snapshot, and overwrites it on every subsequent build. After a suspected build compromise nobody can fetch the artifact that was actually deployed, because the tag now points at a newer image and no immutable version tag or digest record was ever published. The attacker's build is indistinguishable from a clean one once the next push completes.

message.text: An attacker reads the HMAC key literal from `lib/insecurity.ts:42` in the source tree. Given any disclosure of the `SecurityAnswers` table, the attacker computes digests offline for a dictionary of likely answers until one matches. The attacker then replays the matching plaintext answer through the reset flow at `routes/resetPassword.ts:41` to take over the account.

message.text: An attacker who lands script in the shop's origin through any stored or reflected XSS reads `document.cookie` and exfiltrates the session token, because `lib/insecurity.ts:192` calls `res.cookie('token', token)` with no options object and therefore no `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, or `SameSite` attribute.

message.text: Any GitHub user can open or edit a pull request and thereby start the pr-compliance workflow, which runs on pull_request_target in the privileged base-repository context and places the organization-administration token ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN into a step environment. Because the trigger is reachable by an unauthenticated internet user rather than only by trusted contributors, a single script-injection or action-compromise defect anywhere in this workflow exposes a credential that administers the whole juice-shop organization, not just this repository.

description.text: Move ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN out of the pull_request_target workflow in pr-compliance.y…

trustBoundaries.rationale: tb-3 assumes workflow runs start only from verified identities on permitted branches, but pull_request_target lets any pull-request author start this privileged run holding an org-admin credential.

message.text: LLM07 — System Prompt Leakage: the chatbot decides whether to reveal the assistant's tool calls purely from the client-set show_tool_calls cookie at frontend/src/app/chatbot/chat-conversation/chat-conversation.component.ts:68, with no role check, even though the component injects LoginGuard. Line 161 stores every streamed deltaToolCalls chunk on the message regardless of that flag, and line 170 persists the whole conversation, so the internal tool names and raw arguments reach the browser unconditionally. Any authenticated shopper who writes show_tool_calls=true in their own cookie jar sees the view that frontend/src/app/administration/administration.component.html:96 presents as an administrator-only toggle.

message.text: LoginComponent declares testingUsername and testingPassword as public string literals at frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:61 and :62, so the credential pair testing@juice-sh.op / IamU**** (17 chars) is compiled into the production JavaScript bundle that every anonymous visitor downloads. Whether that account exists on the server is not observable from this component, but the literal is a reusable credential shipped to untrusted clients and available to anyone who reads the bundle.

message.text: On every connection the handler iterates the process-global notifications cache and emits each entry to the new socket at line 30, with no filter for the recipient. Each notification object carries a flag property, as the findIndex destructuring at line 34 shows, so a client receives the flag values of challenges solved by other users of the same deployment.

message.text: An attacker scripts unlimited POST requests against /rest/user/login, which server.ts:596 registers with the login handler and no rate-limiting middleware, unlike the reset-password and 2FA routes; each attempt runs a raw database query, so the attacker both brute-forces credentials and saturates the single-threaded server with database work.

description.text: Rate-limit and lock out repeated authentication attempts

message.text: An attacker repeatedly authenticates or replays distinct valid tokens so that lib/insecurity.ts:74 inserts a new entry into tokenMap on every call; the map has no size cap, no expiry sweep, and no eviction, so the resident set of the single Node.js process grows until the container is killed and the shop goes offline for all users.

description.text: Rate-limit expensive requests and bound input size

message.text: An authenticated attacker sends a true-client-ip header containing thousands of nested pseudo-tags; routes/saveLoginIp.ts:25 passes it to sanitizeSecure, which recurses at lib/insecurity.ts:66 once per sanitisation pass with no depth or length limit, driving the call stack to a RangeError outside the handler's try block at line 30.

description.text: Bound sanitizeSecure iteration and input length

message.text: Each accepted connection runs the notifications.forEach replay at line 29 and registers four event handlers, and nothing caps how many connections one client opens or how fast it opens them. An attacker loops unauthenticated handshakes against port 3000, and because the Socket.IO server shares the Node process and event loop with the REST API, the serialization and emit work plus the retained socket state degrade the whole application.

description.text: Rate-limit expensive requests and bound input size

message.text: An operator revokes a user's accounting role in the database, but lib/insecurity.ts:157 decides the accounting authorisation purely from decodedToken.data.role carried inside the already-issued JWT, so the demoted user keeps passing the isAccounting guard until their token expires up to six hours later.

description.text: Enforce correct server-side authorization

trustBoundaries.rationale: The boundary assumes issued tokens encode the user's verified identity and role, but the guard trusts that encoded role indefinitely instead of revalidating it against the database.

message.text: An attacker registers wallet addresses he does not control through the contractExploitListener route, then waits for any of those addresses to trigger the on-chain ContractExploited event. The listener at routes/web3Wallet.ts:27 gates the privilege solely on membership in walletsConnected, a set populated from unauthenticated request bodies, so the attacker is granted the exploit credit earned by a third party's wallet.

description.text: Enforce object-level (ownership) authorization

trustBoundaries.rationale: The tb-1 authorization leg assumes each accessed resource is checked against the authenticated user's identity; this decision uses only a wallet address supplied earlier by an unauthenticated request body.

message.text: The exposed key/secret is the same one the server trusts, so a token signed with it (or the leaked credential) is accepted as authentic.
